subject: Week 32: joint attention emerging - point, name, pause
bodyText:
This week
At the 32-week mark mobility is substantial - many infants crawl or scoot, some skip crawling entirely, and cruising remains an early-mover attainment against a 12-month CDC checkpoint. The headline is joint attention emerging: he follows your gaze and your point, the shared-reference skill that naming and first words are built on. He imitates speech sounds and uses his voice deliberately to get your attention.

Watch-fors this week
- [low concern] Pulling up and toppling on carpet - bruise-grade falls with instant recovery are part of the acquisition curve.
- [low concern] Holiday schedule chaos degrading naps for a few days - expect a reset within a week of routine resuming.
- [monitor] No joint attention by 9-10 months - not following your point or gaze is an early flag for atypical development; raise it at the 9-month visit rather than waiting.
- [call within 24h] Ear-pulling with fever, or any new illness that is not clearly improving.
- [call now] A fall with loss of consciousness, blue lips, or severe respiratory distress - call 911.

Enrichment opportunities
- Point and name a dozen times a day - look, a dog - then pause and wait for his eyes to follow your finger to the target; this is the joint-attention rep, and it is the highest-value daily ritual of the month. CDC 9-month milestones: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/9-months.html
- Ask where-is questions during the daily 30 minutes of reading and accept a look or a hand-swipe as the answer - he is mapping receptive vocabulary months before speech arrives. AAP early literacy: https://www.aap.org/en/patient-care/early-childhood/early-literacy/
- Screen the holiday present haul before it reaches the floor: button batteries and loose small magnets are the two ER-grade hazards, and grandparent presents often predate current safety standards - tape battery compartments and bin anything that fits through a toilet-paper tube.
- Lock in the single paid weekly swim slot before the conversion window closes at day 240: La Petite Baleen rolls enrollment automatically at $130-138 a month, and JCCSF Water Babies caps waitlists at five, so check for openings rather than queue. One program only - there is no dose-response evidence under 12 months. La Petite Baleen tuition: https://www.swimlpb.com/swim-classes/tuition

Upcoming
- Day 252-280 (Jan 18-Feb 15, 2027): 9-month well visit - final call to book; the window opens Jan 18 and includes influenza #2 (first season), an iron rescreen, and possibly an ASQ-3 screen. Bring the joint-attention and motor notes.
- Day 229-235 (week of Dec 26, 2026): quiet holiday stretch - a good week to finish the pre-9-month babyproofing list (anchors, gates, cabinet locks) before the January visit conversation.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Uses fingers to 'rake' food toward herself
  AAP window: day 210-270
  What to look for: Pre-pincer grasp. Coincides with starting finger foods.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/9-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/uses-fingers-rake/complete

- Crawls on hands and knees, or scoots
  AAP window: day 210-330
  What to look for: Some babies skip crawling and go straight to cruising — that is within normal range.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/crawls/complete

- Moves from sitting into a crawl or lie-down position
  AAP window: day 210-330
  What to look for: Postural transition. Predicts comfortable independent exploration.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/gets-from-sit-to-crawl/complete

- Cries or protests when a parent leaves the room
  AAP window: day 210-365
  What to look for: Peak separation anxiety. Healthy attachment, even when it makes drop-off hard.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/cries-when-parent-leaves/complete

- Catches himself with his arms when tipping over while sitting
  AAP window: day 210-300
  What to look for: Protective arm extension — reaching out to break a sideways or forward topple. Makes independent sitting safe enough for hands-busy play.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Movement-8-to-12-Months.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/catches-self-when-sitting/complete
